m: To summarize and state again the main points.
t: Same as « récapituler ».

m: Owing thanks or having a duty to someone.
e: Old English behealdan (to hold, observe); past participle of behold.
t: « Redevable » to someone. Beholden to donors.

m: A group of similar things close together.
t: Un « amas ». A cluster of stars.

m: Logical and consistent; clear.
t: Same as « cohérent ».

m: To think deeply; to consider as a possibility.
t: « Contempler » a view, but also envisager: contemplate resigning.

m: Clever at achieving aims by deceit.
t: Craft = skill, and slyness. A crafty fox.

m: To take apart; to abolish gradually.
e: Old French desmanteler (to strip off a cloak).
t: Same as « démanteler »: take off the mantle.

m: To go without; to give up.
t: Not « forego » (to precede). Forgo dessert = renoncer au dessert.

m: Impossible to pass through or understand.
t: Same as « impénétrable ».

m: Unable to be taken away from or given away.
t: Same as « inaliénable »: les droits inaliénables.

m: Having no skill; clumsy.
t: Opposite of apt. An inept manager = « incapable ».

m: Excessive interest in oneself.
e: Greek Narkissos, mythical youth in love with his reflection.
t: Same as « narcissisme ».

m: A harsh rebuke.
t: Cousin of « objurguer » (rare in French). Think « injure »: a severe scolding.

m: Acceptable but not outstanding; (of a road) able to be travelled.
t: Same as « passable » (just OK). A passable meal.

m: Able to pass through; showing keen insight.
t: Same as « pénétrant »: a penetrating question.

m: Visually attractive, as in a painting.
t: Same as « pittoresque ».

m: To throw back light; to think carefully.
t: Same as « réfléchir »: both meanings (mirror, thought).

m: Having the ability to find quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties.
t: « Débrouillard ».

m: To reduce costs or spending.
t: Cut back: « retrancher ». Retrenchment = austérité.

m: Allowing oneself to enjoy pleasures or luxuries.
t: Indulgence: you pardon yourself everything. « Laxiste envers soi ».

m: To form a theory without firm evidence; to invest at risk.
t: Same as « spéculer ».

m: To forcibly put an end to; to prevent from being seen.
t: Same as « supprimer / réprimer ».

m: Forming a remnant of something that once existed.
t: Same as « vestige »: a vestigial organ.

m: To give or grant; to be consistent with.
e: Old French acorder, Latin ad cor (to the heart).
t: Same as « accorder / être en accord ».

m: Created for a particular purpose only.
t: Same as « ad hoc ».

m: Including everything; comprehensive. (Standard spelling: all-encompassing.)
t: GregMat’s spelling has a typo: the correct form is all-encompassing. « Qui englobe tout ».

m: A standard against which things can be measured.
e: From a surveyor’s bench mark cut in stone.
t: Same in French business jargon: « un benchmark ».

m: Spoiled or ruined; stricken by disease (plants).
t: A blight: la rouille. Blighted hopes.

m: In a state of peaceful happiness; satisfied. (Stress: conTENT.)
t: Same as « content ». Two words: CONtent (the substance) vs conTENT (satisfied).

m: Causing unease or confusion.
t: Same as « déconcertant ».

m: A natural ease; a place or equipment for an activity.
t: Facility for languages = facilité. But a research facility = une installation.

m: Active only in short bursts; irregular.
t: Fits and starts: fitful sleep = sommeil agité.

m: To encourage or stir up (violence or hatred).
t: Same as « inciter ».

m: To persuade; to bring about.
t: Same as « induire » (en erreur). Induce sleep = provoquer le sommeil.

m: An inappropriate remark or expression; unhappiness.
t: Opposite of felicity. An infelicity of style = formule malheureuse.

m: Able to be understood.
t: Same as « intelligible ».

m: Former.
t: A onetime champion = ancien champion.

m: Exploiting circumstances for immediate advantage.
t: Same as « opportuniste ».

m: Seeming reasonable or probable.
t: Same as « plausible ».

m: Behaviour intended to impress or mislead.
t: Une « posture » (not neutral): political posturing = jeu de rôle.

m: Having great power or strong effect.
t: Same as « potentiel / puissant ». A potent drug.

m: Not needed; superfluous.
t: Same as « redondant »; also “laid off” in British English.

m: Too important to be changed.
t: Same as « sacro-saint ».

m: Having sharp judgement, especially in business.
t: A shrewd negotiator = fin négociateur.

m: Plain; without decoration.
t: « Sans fard »: the unadorned truth.

m: Serving as a farewell.
t: Vale! Valedictorian gives the farewell speech.

m: Justified or necessary.
t: Warrant ~ garantir: warranted = guaranteed to be justified.

m: Having a feeling of vague longing.
t: Wishful, melancholy: « nostalgique ».

m: To regard something as belonging to or caused by.
t: Same as « attribuer ».

m: Causing great damage.
t: Same as « calamiteux ».

m: Showing skill with hands or mind.
t: Dexter = right. Cousin of « dextérité ».

m: A formal pronouncement; a short statement of principle.
t: Same as « dicton ». Dictum = a said thing.

m: Conscientiously obedient.
t: Full of duty (devoir): a dutiful son.

m: To happen afterwards, as a result.
t: Same as « s'ensuivre ».

m: To understand after much thought.
e: Old English fæthm (outstretched arms), a unit of depth.
t: Sound the depth: « sonder ». I can’t fathom it.

m: Open, honest and direct.
t: Same as « franc »: Franc de port.

m: To complain in a bad-tempered way.
t: Grommeler. Grumble about taxes.

m: Unwilling to accept new ideas; rigidly conventional.
t: Skin too tight: un esprit « borné ».

m: A person who pretends to have virtues they do not possess.
t: Same as « hypocrite »: an actor playing a role.

m: Unwise; failing to take account of consequences.
t: Not rude: politic = prudent. An impolitic remark = une maladresse.

m: A person who acts as a link between parties.
t: Same as « intermédiaire ».

m: Accepting what happens without active response.
t: Same as « passif ».

m: To walk for pleasure; to talk at length confusedly.
e: Middle Dutch rammelen (to roam in sexual excitement).
t: A rambling speech = discours décousu. Walkers ramble too.

m: To feel bitter indignation at.
f: en vouloir à, ne pas supporter
t: Ressentir ≠ resent: English = bitter. « Il m'en veut » = he resents me.

m: Remaining after the main part has gone.
t: Same as « résiduel ».

m: A substitute, especially a person acting for another.
t: Same as « substitut »: surrogate mother = mère porteuse.

m: Stubbornly determined; intentional.
t: Willful neglect = négligence volontaire; a willful child = têtu.

m: Not genuine; fake.
e: American slang, early 20th century, possibly from fawney (a gilt brass ring used in scams).
t: Holden Caulfield: phoney. « Bidon ».
